checks: The revised raw JSON is exactly the previous reviewed raw JSON with one insertion, 'finitely many' before the mass-Q caps in group i. Its candidate ID, proof, source locators, and dependencies are byte-identical.

The primary source 1a7cfa3d1047cbae §§1–2 assumes a finite covering construction. Accepted 9ee0d9a1e9f65259 uses the finite-cover setting of 5efc62439ac46cfb. Finite cap weights make the sum of the fixed-cap first expansions uniform across the cap group, give a finite sum of continuous increasing inverses and a finite tuple of simultaneous selector choices, and supply common local continuation estimates by taking bounds over the caps. The exact original proof therefore applies with the inserted quantifier.

Matched 1a7cfa3d1047cbae §§1–2, (1)–(4), and 8f0725a173821a00 §2, (7)–(10), with both raw source digests verified. The finite-contact coefficient is the former source's exact expression, and the latter explicitly gives the log-normalization and singleton terms. The later dual or descent assertions in those notes are outside the frozen lemma.

The uniform radial displacement bound places the nearby canonical hulls in the common positive neighborhood. On a compact neighborhood containing these bodies, L has a positive minimum and h is bounded, so the raw logarithm expansion is uniform. The combination (1−tc)L+t(h+cL) is concave for small t≥0. Differentiation of the normalization exponent uses zero old log integral, the signed shell derivative −∫log L v, and the integral of h/L, giving s(v)−H(h). Its contribution to the fixed-mark log derivative is s(v)+h/L−H(h).

Using dot M=−D, dot E=−C_a, and old Gamma(u_ij)=1 gives dot log f=[s(v)+h/L−H(h)−C_a/E_a+D/M]/N. The moving norm term is (D−J_i)/(2M) plus the weighted old norm gradient applied to dot u_ij. Subtracting epsilon times the product derivative gives the coefficient of D as −(1/N+1/2)=−(N+2)/(2N), C_a and J_i with positive signs, s and h/L with negative signs, and H(h) positive. The affine part gives the weighted normal velocity at the contact.

Uniform expansion with a continuous coefficient holds on compact own-interior neighborhoods at the fixed bases by the accepted uniform energy expansion and the uniform raw log expansion. All old zeros are available for the upper bound. A current minimizing mark localizes to the finite set, hence eventually lies inside an old own fiber. Old nonnegativity at the new marks and coefficient continuity give the matching lower bound. This uses a one-sided derivative and requires no spatial derivative of L at a mark.

Checked the proper-plane coarea loss and both supporting hinge signs against the profile-independent radial shell proof. Positive-area inside supporting faces keep their whole-fiber body loss and add a nonnegative hinge; removing that hinge gives the displayed conservative loss. Outside faces retain the negative hinge, and supporting sections of lower dimension give zero surface contribution. Endpoint counting gives the same terms when d=1.

Both loss maps increase by at least S_ij times the increment in threshold speed and are continuous onto the real line. The weighted sum of inverses is strictly increasing onto the real line. Thus equality at a fixed budget is unique, raises the common loss as the budget increases, and preserves the conservative ordering. With finitely many contacts a smallest A_ia is attained and gives exactly the minimum of the equalized conservative responses.

For fixed outside selectors the cap branch has affine slope S_ij+∫theta/||u_ij||>0 and all remaining terms linear in the direction. Each such branch dominates the conservative loss function. Pointwise hinge sign selectors at the solved thresholds give equality simultaneously, yielding an infimum of linear responses over selectors and contacts. This proves concavity in the joint direction. The old proper sections supply local inverse bounds, and the uniform moving-shell expansion determines the actual first losses of the continued caps. At an assigned current point the weighted buffered thresholds dominate the weighted continued thresholds, so at least one individual buffered cap has mass at most the common continued mass.

dependencies.mapping: The fixed bases, uniform O(t) signed radial displacement and almost-everywhere first inward speeds give its signed shell and marked-energy expansions. The old marks admit compact own-interior neighborhoods, so it provides uniform energy variation, continuity of the coefficient and the mass and covariance derivatives. Its shell proof also applies to the fixed continuous integrand log L on the common compact neighborhood.

Use its shell, coarea and inverse proof with the old caps, finite weights, positive proper coareas, signed radial path and independent affine speeds. The section/shell computation and monotone inverse argument do not involve the body-tied profile. Replace that application's scalar contact budget by the independently proved full-space budget min_a A_ia. The selector branch formula then has the same outside selector in its slope, moment and body term.
